ip_top_stories.title: Judge Signals Getty Could Fortify Copyright Claims Against Stability AI
ip_top_stories.summary: A judge has signalled that Getty Images may be able to strengthen its copyright infringement claims against Stability AI, in a significant development in one of the most closely watched AI copyright cases. The ruling relates to the standard for proving watermark intent and could have broad implications for how AI image generators are held liable for training on copyrighted material.

ip_top_stories.title: Delhi High Court orders Copyright Office to rule on Stephen Thaler AI artwork plea in 8 weeks
ip_top_stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has ordered India's Copyright Office to issue a decision within eight weeks on AI pioneer Stephen Thaler's application seeking copyright protection for AI-generated artwork. The case directly tests whether AI-created works can receive copyright protection under Indian law, and comes as Thaler simultaneously pursues a lawsuit against the Indian government over the copyright deadlock.

ip_top_stories.title: Unclear legal landscape for AI spawns licensing as US sees 100 copyright cases
ip_top_stories.summary: With over 100 AI-related copyright cases now active in US courts, the legal uncertainty is driving a wave of licensing agreements between AI companies and rights holders. The report examines how the absence of clear judicial or legislative guidance is reshaping the market for content licensing in the AI era.

ip_top_stories.title: Northern District of California Court Holds State Tort and Contract Claims Not Preempted by Federal Copyright Act, Remands Reddit v. Anthropic to State Court
ip_top_stories.summary: A California federal court has ruled that state tort and contract claims brought by Reddit against Anthropic are not preempted by the federal Copyright Act, remanding the case to state court. The decision is significant for AI litigation strategy, potentially opening additional legal avenues for plaintiffs beyond federal copyright claims.

ip_top_stories.title: Who Owns the Rights to AI Derivatives From Licensing Deals?
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis of the unresolved intellectual property questions arising when AI companies license copyrighted content for training — specifically, who owns the derivative outputs and downstream works generated by models trained on that licensed material. The piece examines how current licensing frameworks may fail to address these complexities.

ip_further_links.title: Stability AI challenges Getty copyright claim over watermark intent standard
ip_further_links.summary: Stability AI is contesting Getty Images' copyright claims by challenging the legal standard used to assess watermark intent, in ongoing litigation over AI training on copyrighted images.

ip_further_links.title: Three YouTube channels file lawsuit against Apple over alleged use of their videos to train AI model
ip_further_links.summary: Three YouTube content creators have filed a copyright lawsuit against Apple alleging their videos were scraped without authorisation to train an AI model.

ip_further_links.title: Disney Deal Shows the Way for Responsible AI Development
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of Disney's AI licensing approach, presented as a model for how content owners and AI developers can reach responsible agreements that respect intellectual property rights.

ip_further_links.title: Premier League criticises UK's new AI copyright rules
ip_further_links.summary: The Premier League has criticised the UK government's proposed AI copyright reforms, arguing they threaten rights holders' ability to control and be compensated for use of their content.

ip_further_links.title: Lights, camera, algorithm: China's AI microdramas go viral — but spark copyright fears
ip_further_links.summary: The rapid proliferation of AI-generated microdramas in China is raising significant copyright concerns as the format scales globally.

ip_further_links.title: The Verge criticises Suno's copyright-infringement guardrails
ip_further_links.summary: The Verge reports that AI music platform Suno's copyright protection measures are inadequate, finding the platform capable of producing close imitations of copyrighted recordings.

ip_further_links.title: The UK Must Choose Between Protecting Creators and Backing Big Tech in AI
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary piece argues that the UK government faces a fundamental choice between protecting creators' intellectual property rights and supporting AI industry interests in its ongoing copyright reform process.

ip_further_links.title: Who owns ideas in the AI age?
ip_further_links.summary: A broad examination of how AI is challenging established concepts of intellectual ownership and what legal frameworks may need to change to address the question of who holds rights over AI-assisted creative and conceptual work.

ip_further_links.title: Supreme Court Ruling Strengthens Legal Shield for AI, Internet Providers, Legal Expert Says
ip_further_links.summary: A legal expert analysis finds that a recent US Supreme Court ruling has reinforced liability protections that could benefit AI companies and internet providers facing copyright and related claims.

ip_further_links.title: AI Rollout Is a People Problem: A Pulse on All Things AI, Part 2
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how the human and organisational dimensions of AI adoption in publishing and research institutions are proving to be the central challenge in rolling out AI tools responsibly.
